skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Creates isolated Git worktrees for feature work, selects a suitable directory, verifies ignore rules, runs project setup, and checks the test baseline.
skill.summary: Create an isolated, verified Git workspace before starting implementation.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented Git commands, dedicated worktree paths, and standard error redirection. However, the skill automatically runs repository-controlled setup and test commands, and it may commit a .gitignore change without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Project setup and test commands can execute repository-controlled scripts and downloaded package code.
remediation.suggestion: Describe each detected command and request explicit approval before execution. Recommend a sandbox and safer package-manager options when available.

remediation.issue: The workflow directs the agent to edit .gitignore and create a commit without explicit user approval.
remediation.suggestion: Show the proposed ignore entry and diff, then request approval before editing or committing. Keep the commit separate from feature work.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution of Repository-Controlled Code
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to run dependency installation, build, and test commands automatically. Package lifecycle scripts, build scripts, and tests can execute arbitrary code from an untrusted repository or dependency.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to auto-detect and run setup, then run project tests. Several listed tools execute repository-defined scripts or package installation hooks.

semantic_findings.title: Unapproved Repository Modification and Commit
semantic_findings.description: When a local worktree directory is not ignored, the skill directs the agent to edit .gitignore and commit the change without requesting approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly lists adding an ignore entry and committing it before proceeding. No confirmation step appears in that branch.

content.value_statement: Concurrent branch work can disrupt the current workspace and hide baseline failures. This skill creates an isolated worktree with directory checks, setup guidance, and test verification.
actual_capabilities: Selects an existing project worktree directory using a defined priority.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a documented worktree directory preference.
Verifies that project-local worktree directories are ignored by Git.
Creates a new branch and linked worktree at the selected location.
Detects common Node.js, Rust, Python, and Go project manifests.
Runs a project-appropriate baseline test and reports the result.
limitations: Requires Git and a repository that supports worktrees.
Uses POSIX shell examples that may need adaptation on Windows.
Setup and test commands require review for each project and trust boundary.
Does not define worktree cleanup, branch integration, or conflict resolution.

use_cases.title: Isolate Feature Development
use_cases.description: Create a separate workspace for a feature while preserving the current branch and working tree.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Agent Tasks
use_cases.description: Give each coding agent a separate branch workspace to reduce file and branch interference.

use_cases.title: Verify a Clean Starting Point
use_cases.description: Install approved dependencies and run baseline tests before implementing a planned change.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated Git worktree for branch <branch-name>. Show the selected location and ask before running setup commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature branch

prompt_templates.title: Follow Repository Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a worktree for <feature>. Check existing worktree directories and CLAUDE.md, verify ignore rules, then propose the creation command.

prompt_templates.title: Establish a Trusted Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for <branch-name>. Identify setup and test commands, explain their effects, request approval, and report baseline results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature work requiring dependency setup and testing

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan isolated worktrees for <task-list>. Avoid branch and path conflicts, validate each destination, and provide a status summary for every task.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced parallel development across several tasks

output_examples.input: Prepare an isolated workspace and verify the baseline.
output: The worktree was created at the approved location.
The detected setup command was approved and completed.
The baseline test suite passed with no failures.

output_examples.input: Set up three worktrees for parallel tasks.
output_examples.output: Prepared distinct destinations and branch names for all three tasks. Each setup and test action remains subject to separate approval.

best_practices: Confirm the worktree destination and branch name before creation.
Verify project-local worktree directories are ignored before adding files.
Review and approve repository setup and test commands before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not create a project-local worktree inside a tracked directory.
Do not run package installation or tests from an untrusted repository without isolation.
Do not continue after baseline failures without explicit user approval.

faq.question: Why use a Git worktree instead of switching branches?
faq.answer: A worktree keeps each branch in a separate directory, preserving current files and reducing context switching.

faq.question: Where does the skill place worktrees?
faq.answer: It prefers an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory, then checks repository guidance, then asks the user.

faq.question: Why must a local worktree directory be ignored?
faq.answer: Ignoring the directory prevents nested worktree contents from appearing as repository changes.

faq.question: Does the skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: The source workflow proposes automatic setup, but users should review and approve commands because package tools may execute project code.

faq.question: What happens when baseline tests fail?
faq.answer: The skill reports the failures and asks whether to investigate or continue.

faq.question: Does the skill remove worktrees after completion?
faq.answer: No. Cleanup and branch integration require a separate workflow.
